brief: The Market Ear compiles cross-bank data arguing systematic flows and buyback support are turning into a headwind just as volatility compresses to unusual extremes. BofA models systematic strategies selling $163bn in a down market versus only $9bn bought in an up market, an asymmetry driven by positioning already being high rather than merely elevated. Deutsche Bank shows vol-control equity allocations maxed at the 100th percentile, leaving no room for further buying. Goldman's one-month conditional projections corroborate this: modest additional buying if markets rise, a violent unwind if markets fall, both globally and in the S&P; Goldman's own estimated systematic length stands at $146.5bn, up ~$2bn week over week and at the upper end of its one-year range. Separately, a strategist (McElligott) calls the collapse in volatility "epic" and warns of possible trading losses. Compounding this, buyback activity is near its peak just as the September blackout window begins expanding, removing a major source of incremental buying. The note reports these data points rather than issuing its own forecast beyond the implied selling risk.
